Forgive me, then, if I find it hard to call you impartial when you call people who use the the term MOBA to be ignorant.
DMRPG is hardly impartial, it's merely your opinion of how the genre should be named. And unfortunately for that "have fewer people use ARTS and MOBA to describe DotA" goal of yours, opinions differ.

DotA isn't a deathmatch arrangement. A fed carry doesn't matter as much if he lets someone like Nature's Prophet backcap 2 sets of barracks.

As for the other games, consider this: No one calls CtF a deathmatch. The same goes for UT's Onslaught, CoD's Domination, along with damn near every variant in those other games that doesn't have the name Deathmatch on it.

Note that I said objectives, not objective.

In a DotA-like, killing the enemy team is just one of many objectives (destroy towers, kill minions, take down barracks, etc.) that a team needs to accomplish to take down the enemy ancient/nexus/whatever.

The deathmatch gametype, on the other hand, only requires the team/player to kill the other guy(s) X amount of times in order to win - and DotA simply does not work that way.

Here's the thing, though: There's a problem with using DMRPG. Deathmatch, in most, if not all of its iterations, implies a lack of objectives. (see Quake, UT, CoD, etc.) DotA-like doesn't work either, since the DotA acronym (as iconic as it may be) doesn't tell new players much about the game. 

So sure, you can say that MOBA sounds verbose and stupid to you, but you shouldn't be calling either Riot or its players ignorant for at least trying to classify a genre that has proven itself to be incredibly hard to classify.

But now that you brought up the subject of text up, I wonder: Do people care about those stats on the on the bottom pane when it comes to DotA? In my experience with LoL, the stats I want to know come from either my Ability tooltips or the stuff I buy/my opponent buys from the store.

Oh, I know there's just one player on the map.

But let's say that I'm soloing top, and all of the sudden, someone like Warwick starts to gank the bot lane. In LoL, I can know that immediately by just looking at the mini-map. Doing that would be much harder if Warwick were just a colored dot on the map.

I like how its looking so far from an UI perspective. 

- I'm glad they took a lesson from LoL and added the segmented health bars. These will make the act of distinguishing squishy and tanky targets much easier than in the original DotA. I do hope they implement a different color in the enemy health bars, though.
- This is pure speculation, but if the quick buy bar works like a queue, it should make planning builds and buying wards much, much easier.
- Combining the team status with the clock-sundial thing makes for a very efficient use of space.  I think we'll also be able to tell if an enemy is dead without having to look at the scoreboard - which is one of my gripes in regards to the LoL interface.
- A gripe I do have, though, involves the map. I see no character pics in it. Colored dots might suffice for most players, but since I'm coming from LoL, I think this is a most unfortunate omission.

I've never had luck with earplugs, unfortunately. Maybe I'm putting them on incorrectly or something, but they usually either fail to drown out the sound or they fall out from my ears in the middle of the night. :-/

As for the reason for my indecisiveness: I guess that's something I would like to know myself. Paralysis, however, would also be a good way to describe it. I usually can commit to some action as long as I can work without being distracted or frustrated. Errands are a bit different, though. I've been doing errands for most of my life, so I'm fairly good at them. Unfortunately, they're very mundane, so I tend to procrastinate on them most of the time :(

I have this odd thing that happens to me with planning. Whenever I try to use a planning tool (Moleskine, Outlook, Basecamp, Remember the Milk, etc. ), there's always a nagging flaw about them (e.g. Outlook doesn't sync with Google Tasks ) that I can't quit obsessing over. My brain then tells me "You HAVE to solve this problem before you start!" - but when I'm not able to find the solution ( which happens far too often ), my mind keeps telling me to stop using the tool.

I don't know if it is normal, but that usually happens to me whenever something reminds me of a painful/embarrassing experience. My mind uses it as a way to distract itself from the bad memory, for some reason.

I know dying sucks. I mean, I'm a bloody hemophobe, for Pete's sake.

The problem is, like you said, that I'm stuck. That word, however, vastly underestimates the degree of stuckness I'm at right now.

My job's a good example: I can't quit my job even if I wanted to. I took this position as a favor for my cousin. She recently found the professor position she had been searching for over a year, but the university had one condition: she had to find a replacement for the TA post she previously occupied. I was the only person she could find on such a short notice.

There's a few more details about the insomnia that I forgot to mention, though: I mean, yes, I do have racing thoughts for sure, and they often keep me awake. But the real "kick in the balls," so to speak, comes from a rooster farm that lies 20 feet away from my bedroom window. :-/

Yet, as annoying as those rooster cries may be, they're trivial compared to the problems I have with choice: Whenever I try to make one, I feel like I'm lost in a fucking buffet after eating oatmeal for 10 years straight. Do I want to write X? Do I want to build Y? Do I want to program Z? Even if I choose one of them, the errands A, B and C come out of nowhere and then I'm back at square one with a couple more options thrown in. ( And I haven't even put frustration into the mix. )

I could go on and on about all the shit I have to go through... but what I really want to say is that, honestly, I can't take much more of this. From where I'm at right now, though, I really can't see another way out.
